module_title: Soil Composition, Chemical Properties, and Sub-divisions
introduction: At this level, we dive into the chemical deficiencies common across Indian soils, the specific behavioral traits of black soil, and the critical distinction between old and new alluvial soils.

core_concepts.title: Khadar vs. Bhangar (Alluvial Divisions)
core_concepts.description: 'Khadar' is NEW alluvium, light in color, finer in texture, and highly fertile as it is renewed yearly by floods. 'Bhangar' is OLD alluvium, darker, less fertile, and contains calcareous nodules called 'Kankar'.

core_concepts.title: The 'Self-Ploughing' Black Soil
core_concepts.description: During the hot summer, black soil develops deep and wide cracks. This allows oxygen to naturally penetrate deep into the soil. When it rains, the soil absorbs water, swells, and becomes extremely sticky, which is why it must be tilled immediately after the first shower.

core_concepts.title: Chemical Composition of Black Soil
core_concepts.description: It is rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime. However, it is generally poor in 'phosphorus', nitrogen, and organic matter.

core_concepts.title: The Process of 'Leaching' (Laterite)
core_concepts.description: Laterite soil is the result of intense 'leaching'. Heavy monsoon rains wash away the silica and lime from the topsoil, leaving behind iron oxide and aluminum, which give the soil its characteristic brick-like quality (the word 'later' means brick in Latin).

important_entities.name: General Indian Soil Deficiency
important_entities.significance: Almost all soils in India (including the fertile Alluvial) are inherently deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Humus. This is why NPK (Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium) and Urea fertilizers are heavily used in Indian agriculture.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Alluvial Soil is NOT Rich in Nitrogen
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Despite being the most fertile soil, Alluvial soil is actually poor in Nitrogen and Humus. It is fertile primarily because it is rich in Potash and is constantly renewed by rivers.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In Hindi, 'Bhangar' refers to scrap or old things. Use this to remember that Bhangar is the OLD alluvial soil, while Khadar is the NEW.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks which soil requires tillage immediately after the first rain because it gets too sticky, the answer is always Black Soil.
The concept of 'Leaching' is exclusively tied to Laterite soil in multiple-choice questions.
